solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note as clever? Not half!

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for 'as' or 'in the capacity of'

indicators.note: not half of the word clever means dropping its first half and keeping only the back three letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a note counts as clever and is told, emphatically, yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as the British exclamation meaning 'very much so', but it tells you to keep only half of 'clever' (VER).
explanation.definitionFit: A musical eighth note, held for half a crotchet, is called by this name in British usage.

clue.text: Ask a gospeller?

parts.note: to ask is to pose a query, a synonym
Mark is one of the four evangelists who wrote a gospel

explanation.surface: A request to put a query to one of the evangelists.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a punctuation symbol is what you put after 'Ask a gospeller', and the clue itself ends with one.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol ending an interrogative sentence is named by joining a word for query with the name of the second evangelist.

clue.text: Twelve syllables and rhymes in verse of old times

definitions.text: Twelve syllables and rhymes in verse of old times

parts.words: Twelve syllables and rhymes in verse of old times
parts.note: describes the classical French line of twelve syllables, used in rhyming couplets by poets of earlier centuries

explanation.surface: A description of a metrical form from poetry of earlier ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue was meant to read 'in a verse', making it twelve syllables itself; the setter confirmed on the blog that the 'a' was dropped by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The French heroic line, named after medieval romances of Alexander the Great, has twelve syllables and usually comes in rhymed couplets.

clue.text: Brute after this part of street tussle

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rough fight on the street, with a brute somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brute' looks like a thug in the fight, but it is Brutus, addressed in Caesar's dying words 'Et tu, Brute?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Caesar says the Latin phrase meaning 'and you' immediately before the name Brute.

clue.text: Find out intramural unexpected wealth

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of find are put out of order

parts.note: intramural literally means within the wall (Latin murus), so it names a wall; the clue means the other letters go inside it

explanation.surface: Discovering that money is to be had inside the walls of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, 'intramural' puts an anagram of FIND within WALL, doing double duty as container and its signal; the WALL letters stay in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden unearned gain, like fruit blown down by the wind, is unexpected wealth.

clue.text: Where lemons may be said to be experienced

indicators.note: may be said signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as a similar-sounding word

parts.note: lemons are found in curd, as in the spread lemon curd

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about where lemons have had their experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon curd is a sweet British spread made of lemons, eggs, butter and sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: To have incurred something, such as a loss or cost, is to have experienced or suffered it.

clue.text: Fille de Septembre, peut-être la femme

parts.note: September perhaps is a month, in French mois
the woman, in French, is she: elle

explanation.surface: A French sentence: a girl of September, perhaps the woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is in French; 'de' is taken as written and 'peut-être' (perhaps) marks September as an example of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a young unmarried lady, a damsel, is a synonym of fille, girl.

clue.text: Attraction of having everyone on the river

parts.note: everyone means all
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: The appeal of having the whole community out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or the power to attract is a synonym for attraction.

clue.text: Lack of rigour by non-professionals boxing

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the lay people surround the other letter

parts.note: the laity are lay people, those not of a profession
by as in multiplication (three by four) is the times sign X

explanation.surface: Amateurs who take up boxing are not strict about their training.
explanation.definitionFit: Slackness or looseness of standards is a lack of rigour.

clue.text: Wash and finally scrub articles

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word scrub

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Instructions to clean up and, at the end, scrub some items.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash oneself or something by immersion in water is a synonym.

clue.text: Loving father's treacle?

parts.note: the word treacle is the Greek heroine's name in a jumbled, tangled form, her name made complicated

explanation.surface: A doting dad's sweet talk, as sugary as syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'treacle' is what you get from ELECTRA when it is made complex, that is, scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalytic term for a daughter's unconscious attachment to her father, after the Greek heroine devoted to Agamemnon.

clue.text: See 10
Side of meat in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means in a mess or muddle, so the letters of meat are jumbled

explanation.surface: A side dish of meat cooked in a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in sport is a group of players, a synonym.

clue.text: For the cat, the mat is trendy

definitions.text: For the cat, the mat is
definitions.meaning: in the reading-primer line 'the cat sat on the mat', the mat is the place the animal was seated
describes whatever is the fashionable centre of things

explanation.surface: A cat's view that its mat is the fashionable place to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters, spaced two ways, give 'where it sat' and the idiom for the fashionable place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the fashionable centre of things serves as a description of anything trendy.

clue.text: Smoother cover for pillow, all stuffing taken out, one wanders

indicators.note: cover for says the smoother word wraps around the letters left from pillow and all

parts.note: sleeker means smoother

indicators.note: the stuffing is the inner letters, so taking it out leaves only the outside letters of pillow and of all

explanation.surface: A smoother pillowcase, emptied of stuffing, and someone who wanders.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'stuffing' of a word is its inner letters, so pillow keeps only P and W, and all keeps A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who walks about while asleep is one who wanders at night.

clue.text: What's sweet as nothing on fixed distance makes us spellbound

parts.note: 'sweet FA' (sweet Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing at all, so FA is what goes with sweet

indicators.note: fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters of distance are re-ordered

explanation.surface: Something sweet, set at a fixed distance, keeps us transfixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Fanny Adams', shortened to sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entranced or held in thrall is a synonym for being spellbound.

clue.text: Freeloader's suffering

indicators.note: free signals that the letters of loader are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: The hardship a sponger endures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freeloader' reads as one word, a sponger, but 'Free' is the anagram signal for LOADER.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful trial or harsh experience is a synonym for suffering.

clue.text: Hare is always among the leaders of leftist existential theatre

indicators.note: among says the word for always sits inside the leading letters
the leaders are the first letters of leftist, existential and theatre

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A hare keeps showing up at the front of avant-garde left-wing theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year is called by this name.

clue.text: What's in deadly mixture? A type of chemical

indicators.note: in says the cry goes inside the scrambled letters
mixture signals the letters of deadly are mixed up

parts.note: eh is a cry of What?, and the 's is 'is', so it is in

explanation.surface: Asking what is in a lethal brew and being told it is a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' gives ALDYDE from DEADLY, with EH placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic compounds with a CHO group, such as formaldehyde, belong to this class of chemical.

clue.text: Thought to be half reckless and poorly done

indicators.note: half of the word reckless, its first four letters
poorly means badly, so the letters of done are put in a bad order

explanation.surface: A judgement that something was rather rash and badly carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoned in the sense of considered or judged is a synonym for 'thought to be'.

clue.text: Flute of champagne first served in cool half-pint, perhaps

indicators.note: half says to keep the first two of the four letters of the word pint
in puts the champagne letter inside the rearranged letters
served as in served up differently, so the letters of cool are re-arranged
first picks the opening letter of champagne

explanation.surface: A glass of champagne served first, in a chilled half-pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flute' looks like a champagne glass, but it is the instrument. 'served' scrambles COOL to COLO, with C put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small, high-pitched member of the woodwind family is a kind of flute.

clue.text: Please supply pass

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, in a supple way, means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A polite request to hand over a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the verb to provide, but here it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by, a synonym.

clue.text: Blanket with a hole once mostly covered in noodle soup

indicators.note: covered in says the shortened word sits inside the soup

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of once

explanation.surface: A blanket that once had a hole and got soaked in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American cloak is a blanket with a hole in the middle for the head.

clue.text: Consider Byzantium partly a city

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to think about the ancient city on the Bosporus.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: This English Midlands place gained city status in 1977.

clue.text: Single awful sin, still? This could describe it

definitions.text: Single awful sin, still? This could describe it

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of sin are put in a dreadful order

parts.note: still in the sense of level or calm means even

explanation.surface: Asking whether one terrible sin still counts, and what term fits it.
explanation.walkthrough: Any single deadly sin is one of the traditional seven; the clue's question is the description.
explanation.definitionFit: There are seven deadly sins, so any one awful sin is a single member of a group of seven.

clue.text: See 1 down
Belly's showing up in porn

indicators.note: showing up in a down light means reading upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: tums is a childish word for bellies; the 's makes the plural

explanation.surface: A bare midriff appearing in adult material.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene or indecent material is a synonym for pornography.

clue.text: "Your excellency, rub my pink dicky", says yokel

parts.note: an excellency is a title holder such as a nobleman, here a count

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A rustic makes an absurd and rude request to a dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky', British slang for shaky or unsound (a dicky heart), scrambles RUB MY PINK into RYBUMPKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsophisticated rural person is a stock synonym for a yokel.

clue.text: See 7
See 27
Got into debt, breaking nearly every word

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters are broken up and rearranged
nearly says the last letter of every is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who got into debt by breaking almost every promise they gave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' gives EVER, and 'breaking' scrambles EVER plus WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking more from a bank account than it holds puts the holder into debt.

clue.text: Extremely strict order expected to be put aside

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of strict, order and expected

explanation.surface: A strict order that something is expected to be kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in reserve for later use has been put aside.
